reading.body:
The only data center fact here is a naming convention: Studio BETA SRLS is a small Italian professional-services firm, not a facility, and the record carries zero megawatts.

The point is tagged telecom=data_center in OpenStreetMap at Porto San Giorgio, on Italy's Adriatic coast. Its name carries two signals against that tag. "SRLS" is the Italian simplified limited-liability form, used by small startups, freelancers, and professional practices because it requires less minimum capital. "Studio" in Italian usage indicates a professional-services or design office. The record has no operator, no website, and no address beyond the city name. The same pattern appears in a similarly named Studio Delta Srl entry elsewhere in the dataset.

This matters for AI because capacity inventories are increasingly assembled from volunteered geographic data, and a tagged point is not a building with power. An entry like this one inflates a count of data centers without adding a single megawatt of load, and the error is invisible unless someone reads the name. The dataset itself treats the entry as a documented mistag rather than fabricating specifications for it, which is the correct handling.

What this record does not tell you is anything about Italian data center capacity, the grid, or AI compute. It is one point, verified only by inference from a corporate suffix and a common noun, with no power figure, no operator, and no independent source beyond an OpenStreetMap tagging review. The nearest airport, Marche Airport at 36 miles, is the only geographic anchor besides the coordinates.
